# Results {#sec-results}

## Centre-point performance and reproducibility {#sec-centre}

@tbl-centre gives the mean, the standard deviation and the coefficient of variation of the centre points of both designs. These replicates carry the variation between runs of the scale-down model and of the methods, and they are the pure error of the lack-of-fit test. High mannose is the least precise attribute at the centre point in both designs, with a coefficient of variation of `{python} pct(CV_HM_S)` in the screening design and `{python} pct(CV_HM_R)` in the response-surface design. That is several times the precision of the glycan map, `{python} pct(float(AMV3010.precision_pct))` of the result (Appendix D), so most of the variation in high mannose comes from the culture. The standard deviation of galactosylation at the centre point is `{python} fx(SD_GA_R)` points in the response-surface design against `{python} fx(SD_GA_S)` in the screening design. Standard deviations from `{python} words(NC_RSM)` and `{python} words(NC_SCR)` runs are imprecise. The larger value enters the lack-of-fit test of the galactosylation model as pure error, which is one reason why that test has the highest p-value of the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` models (@sec-models).

```{python}
#| output: asis
_hdr = [[C("Attribute", rs=2), C("Screening design", cs=4), C("Response-surface design", cs=4)],
        ["n", "Mean", "SD", "CV (%)", "n", "Mean", "SD", "CV (%)"]]
_body = []
for _r in RESPS:
    _a, _b = CCV_S.loc[D.RESP_LABEL[_r]], CCV_R.loc[D.RESP_LABEL[_r]]
    _body.append([ANAME[_r], str(int(_a["n"])), T.num(_a["Mean"]), T.num(_a["SD"]), f"{_a['%CV']:.1f}",
                  str(int(_b["n"])), T.num(_b["Mean"]), T.num(_b["SD"]), f"{_b['%CV']:.1f}"])
CTable(header=_hdr, body=_body, align="lrrrrrrrr",
       caption="Mean, standard deviation and coefficient of variation of the centre points of the two designs, "
               "as measured in the scale-down model.", label="tbl-centre").show()
```

## Screening: factor effects {#sec-screening}

@tbl-screening lists the effects significant at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` for each attribute, as the change in the attribute across the range studied of the factor. The screening models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in SCR_NSIG_MODEL])` have no significant model F-test (p `{python} pfmt(SCRF['afucosylation']['p'])` and p `{python} pfmt(SCRF['high_mannose']['p'])`), so their individual effects identify candidates and no more. No attribute shows significant curvature in the screening design, with lack-of-fit p-values from `{python} fx(SCR_LOF_MIN, 3)` to `{python} fx(SCR_LOF_MAX, 3)`, but with `{python} words(SDF_PE)` degrees of freedom for pure error that test detects only a large curvature.

pCO2 has the largest effect on acidic variants, which fall by `{python} fx(abs(eff('acidic_variants', LTR['co2'])))` points from the low to the high end of its range. A higher culture pH also lowers acidic variants, and a higher culture temperature raises them. Culture duration has the largest effect on galactosylation, a fall of `{python} fx(abs(eff('galactosylation', LTR['duration'])))` points, and the interaction of culture pH with culture duration is nearly as large and of opposite sign. A higher pCO2 and a higher culture pH lower galactosylation, and a higher culture temperature raises it. A higher culture pH and a longer culture raise aggregate, by `{python} fx(eff('aggregates_hmw', LTR['pH']))` and `{python} fx(eff('aggregates_hmw', LTR['duration']))` points. A higher culture pH raises high mannose and a higher culture temperature lowers it. Afucosylation falls with a longer culture, and its interactions of culture pH with culture duration and with pCO2 are significant.

A higher osmolality lowers galactosylation by `{python} fx(abs(eff('galactosylation', OSM_L)))` points (p `{python} pfmt(pef('galactosylation', OSM_L))`) and acidic variants by `{python} fx(abs(eff('acidic_variants', OSM_L)))` points (p `{python} pfmt(pef('acidic_variants', OSM_L))`) across its range, and its interactions with `{python} join_and([_short(INV_LTR[[c for c in t if c != OSM_L][0]]) for t in OSM_INT_GA])` are significant for galactosylation. Under PCP-003 §6.3 osmolality should therefore have been carried into the response-surface design, with the design amended before execution. It was not (DEV-003-03, osmolality left out of the response-surface design). The osmolality study later measured its effect at the least favourable NOR combination for acidic variants (@sec-osmolality).

Screening run 4 ran below its design setting of pCO2, because the pCO2 probe read high (DEV-003-01, pCO2 probe drift). It is analysed at its recorded setting of `{python} pv('co2', R4_REC)`, and the set of significant effects in @tbl-screening is the same with the run at its design setting (@sec-dev-01). The screening model identifies effects. The response-surface model is the predictive model of this step, and it re-estimates the effects of the `{python} words(len(FS))` factors carried forward in a design without aliases.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_neg = lambda v: T.num(v).replace("-", "−")
_cap = lambda s_: s_ if (s_[:1] == "p" and s_[1:2].isupper()) else cap1(s_)
_rows = []
for _r in RESPS:
    _e = SCRE[_r]
    for _, _x in _e[_e["p-value"] < ALPHA].iterrows():
        _rows.append([ANAME[_r], _cap(tname(lt_term(_x["Term"]))), _neg(_x["Effect"]), p3(_x["p-value"])])
_scr = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Term", "Effect", "p-value"])
T.frame(_scr, f"Effects significant at α = {ALPHA:g} in the screening design. The effect is the change in the "
        "attribute across the range studied of the factor, as measured in the scale-down model.",
        "tbl-screening", merge=["Attribute"], header={"Effect": "Effect\n(points)"},
        align=["P{3.6cm}", "P{5.8cm}", "r", "r"]).show()
```

## Response-surface models {#sec-rsm}

### Selected models and their adequacy {#sec-models}

@tbl-models gives the selected model of each attribute on all `{python} N_ALL` runs. The raw scale is used for `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in RAWR])`, and the log scale for `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in LOGR])`. For afucosylation the Box-Cox interval excludes both 0 and 1, so the rule keeps the raw scale although the profile does not support it either (@sec-residuals). Every selected model meets the model F-test (p < 0.001 for every model), the lack-of-fit test (p from `{python} fx(P_LOF_MIN, 3)` to `{python} fx(P_LOF_MAX, 3)`) and the limit on overfitting, with predicted R² at most `{python} fx(GAP_MAX, 3)` below R² against the limit of `{python} fx(GAPMAX)`.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for _r in RESPS:
    _f = FIT[_r]
    _bc = _f["boxcox"]
    _rows.append([ANAME[_r], "log" if _r in LOGR else "raw",
                  f"{_bc['lambda']:.2f} ({_bc['lo']:.2f} to {_bc['hi']:.2f})".replace("-", "−"),
                  str(len(_f["names"])), f"{_f['R2']:.3f}", f"{_f['adjR2']:.3f}", f"{_f['predR2']:.3f}",
                  f"{_f['gap']:.3f}", p3(_f["p"]), p3(_f["p_lof"])])
_mt = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Scale", "Box-Cox λ (95 % interval)", "Terms", "R²", "Adj. R²",
                                   "Pred. R²", "R² minus pred. R²", "F-test p", "Lack of fit p"])
T.frame(_mt, f"Selected response-surface models of the production bioreactor on all {N_ALL} runs, against the "
        "model F-test, the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting.", "tbl-models",
        header={"Box-Cox λ (95 % interval)": "Box-Cox λ\n(95 % interval)", "R² minus pred. R²": "R² minus\npred. R²",
                "Lack of fit p": "Lack of\nfit p", "F-test p": "F-test\np", "Adj. R²": "Adj.\nR²", "Pred. R²": "Pred.\nR²"},
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "l", "P{2.5cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Terms are counted without the intercept and the block term. Adj. R², adjusted R². Pred. R², "
                    "predicted R² from PRESS. The model scale is the log scale where the 95 % interval of the Box-Cox "
                    "exponent λ contains 0 and excludes 1, and the raw scale otherwise.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

At the set-points, the selected models of afucosylation and acidic variants predict `{python} pct(CBIAS['afucosylation']['pred'], 2)` and `{python} pct(CBIAS['acidic_variants']['pred'], 2)` in the scale-down model. The means of the `{python} words(CBIAS['afucosylation']['n'])` centre points of the response-surface design are `{python} pct(CBIAS['afucosylation']['mean'], 2)` and `{python} pct(CBIAS['acidic_variants']['mean'], 2)`, with standard errors of `{python} fx(CBIAS['afucosylation']['se'])` and `{python} fx(CBIAS['acidic_variants']['se'])` points. The lack-of-fit test is not significant for either model. For acidic variants the difference lies in the unfavourable direction, since a model that predicts too high near the set-point overstates the distance to the lower limit there.

@tbl-reeval-bioreactor sets the plan's full quadratic model, fitted on the raw scale to the planned runs and to all runs with a block term, beside the model used. On the planned runs the full quadratic models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in AUGR])` exceed the limit on overfitting, which is why the design was augmented. On all runs the full quadratic model of acidic variants meets the limit, but that of high mannose still exceeds it, with predicted R² `{python} fx(HM_FULLA_GAP, 2)` below R². The selected model of high mannose meets the limit, and the full quadratic model that the plan prescribes would leave high mannose without an adequate model on all runs.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.model_reevaluation("bioreactor").show()
```

### Residual patterns and influential runs {#sec-residuals}

The selected models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in RI_PASS])` meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs, and those of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in RI_FAIL])` do not (@tbl-crit4). For these two the regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values has a significant slope, `{python} join_and([f"p {pfmt(RI[r]['p_spread'])} for {OUT[r]}" for r in SPREAD])`, so the spread of their residuals grows with the predicted value. No model shows a trend with the run order, and the lowest p-value of that test is `{python} fx(P_ORD_MIN, 3)`. No run has a Cook's distance above the median of F(p, n − p) of its model, which lies between `{python} fx(min(F_LIM), 3)` and `{python} fx(max(F_LIM), 3)` for these models. Every model has at least one run above `{python} f"{COOKF:g}"`/n = `{python} fx(COOK_LIM, 3)`, with `{python} N_FLAG` flags on `{python} len(FLAG_RUNS)` runs in all.

Each flagged run was deleted in turn and the model selection repeated. For every attribute and every deleted run, the model selected without the run met the model F-test, the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting, the conclusion over the NOR was the same as with all runs, and every NOR-propagated PAR still contained the NOR. The share of the region studied that lies inside the design space ranged from `{python} pct(100 * min(DS_DEL))` to `{python} pct(100 * max(DS_DEL))`, against `{python} pct(100 * DSG['fraction'])` with all runs. The same model was selected in `{python} N_FLAG_SAME` of the `{python} N_FLAG` cases. For afucosylation, `{python} INFL_CHG['afucosylation'][0]`. For high mannose, `{python} INFL_CHG['high_mannose'][0]`. For acidic variants, `{python} join_and(INFL_CHG['acidic_variants'])`. The deletions cover the conclusions over the NOR, the PARs and the design space. The capability of @sec-capability comes from the integrated model and does not depend on these runs.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for _r in RESPS:
    _ri = RI[_r]
    _rows.append([ANAME[_r], p3(_ri["p_spread"]), p3(_ri["p_order"]), f"{_ri['cook_max']:.3f} ({_ri['cook_run']})",
                  f"{_ri['f_limit']:.3f}", ", ".join(str(_x["run"]) for _x in INFL[_r]),
                  "met" if _ri["met"] else "not met"])
_c4 = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Spread p", "Order p", "Largest Cook's distance (run)", "F median",
                                   "Runs above 4/n", "Verdict"])
T.frame(_c4, "Residual patterns and influential runs of the selected models, against the criterion on residuals "
        "and influential runs.", "tbl-crit4",
        header={"Spread p": "Spread\np", "Order p": "Order\np",
                "Largest Cook's distance (run)": "Largest Cook's\ndistance (run)", "F median": "Median of\nF(p, n − p)",
                "Runs above 4/n": "Runs above\n4/n"},
        align=["P{3.3cm}", "r", "r", "l", "r", "P{2.3cm}", "l"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Spread, the regression of the absolute residuals on the predicted values. Order, the regression "
                    "of the residuals on the run order, the augmentation runs continuing the planned order. A run above "
                    f"4/n = {COOK_LIM:.3f} for {N_ALL} runs is examined by deletion, and the model fails the criterion "
                    "only on a significant slope or on a run above the median of F(p, n − p), where p is the number of "
                    "parameters of the model.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The two significant growths of the residual spread were sized against the criterion of each attribute. For galactosylation the residual standard deviation is `{python} fx(SPRD['galactosylation']['sd_lo'])` points in the lower half of the predicted values and `{python} fx(SPRD['galactosylation']['sd_hi'])` points in the upper half, nearly the same. For acidic variants it is `{python} fx(SPRD['acidic_variants']['sd_lo'], 3)` and `{python} fx(SPRD['acidic_variants']['sd_hi'], 3)` on the log scale, so the spread at the low end of the predictions, where the lower limit decides, is smaller than the pooled estimate. With the standard deviation of the half in which each prediction lies, the judgement over the NOR gives the same conclusion for both attributes. For acidic variants the lowest prediction limit moves from `{python} pct(WCA['pi_low'], 2)` to `{python} pct(SPRD['acidic_variants']['lo'], 2)`, still below the lower limit. Afucosylation, whose Box-Cox profile rejects the raw scale but whose growth of spread is not significant (p `{python} pfmt(RI['afucosylation']['p_spread'])`), has a residual standard deviation of `{python} fx(SPRD['afucosylation']['sd_lo'])` points in the lower half and `{python} fx(SPRD['afucosylation']['sd_hi'])` in the upper half. Judged with the standard deviation of each half, it still meets its criterion across the NOR, with prediction limits from `{python} pct(SPRD['afucosylation']['lo'], 2)` to `{python} pct(SPRD['afucosylation']['hi'], 2)`.

The normal quantile plots of the residuals in @fig-diag-afucosylation to @fig-diag-aggregates show the residuals close to the line, with no marked departure from normality, so the normality criterion is met. Each figure also plots the standardized residuals against the predicted values and the predicted against the measured values, on the scale of the model.

### Effects of the parameters {#sec-effects}

The coefficients of the selected models are in coded units, so each measures the change from the set-point to the end of the range of its factor. Appendix C gives the coefficient tables of afucosylation, galactosylation, high mannose and aggregate, and @tbl-coef-acidic and @tbl-anova-acidic those of acidic variants, the attribute nearest its limit. @tbl-effect-size states each main effect as the change it causes across the range studied, at manufacturing scale with the other factors at their set-points, against the width of the criterion.

PCP-003 §7 calls an effect practically important when that change is large relative to the width of the criterion, and neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a threshold. This report reads a change of a fifth of the width or more as large, of a tenth to a fifth as moderate and of less than a tenth as small, and these bands are its own. Read so, the effects of `{python} EFF_TXT['large']` are large. The effects of `{python} EFF_TXT['moderate']` are moderate, and those of `{python} EFF_TXT['small']` are small. Only for acidic variants do the effects bring the attribute to its limit within the NOR, and there the large effects of pCO2 and culture pH set the edges of its PARs (@sec-par-table).

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for _e in EFF:
    _rows.append([ANAME[_e["resp"]], _cap(_short(_e["factor"])), f"{_e['d']:.2f}".replace("-", "−"),
                  f"{_e['d_nor']:.2f}".replace("-", "−"), f"{_e['width']:.3g}", f"{_e['share']:.1f}", BAND(_e["share"])])
_ef = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Parameter", "Change over the range studied", "Change over the NOR",
                                   "Criterion width", "Share of the width (%)", "Size"])
T.frame(_ef, "Main effects of the selected models against the width of each criterion, at manufacturing scale "
        "with the other factors at their set-points.", "tbl-effect-size", merge=["Attribute"],
        header={"Change over the range studied": "Change over the\nrange studied", "Change over the NOR": "Change over\nthe NOR",
                "Criterion width": "Criterion\nwidth", "Share of the width (%)": "Share of the\nwidth (%)"},
        align=["P{2.6cm}", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "l"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Main effects only, for the parameters in each selected model. Changes and widths in percentage points. "
                    "Size, the report's own bands: large from a fifth of the width, moderate from a tenth, small below a "
                    "tenth. The aggregate criterion has an upper limit only, and its width is taken from 0.")],
        notes_per_row=True).show()
```

Afucosylation falls as culture duration, culture pH, culture temperature and pCO2 rise. The interaction of culture pH with culture duration is as large as the main effect of culture duration and of opposite sign. At the low end of the pH range a longer culture lowers afucosylation by `{python} fx(abs(DUR_AF_LO))` points across the range of culture duration, and at the high end of the pH range it changes it by `{python} fx(abs(DUR_AF_HI))` points. The squared term of culture pH is negative, so with the other factors at their set-points afucosylation is highest inside the pH range and falls toward both ends.

Galactosylation falls with culture duration, pCO2 and culture pH, and rises with culture temperature. Culture pH changes the size of each of these effects. Across the range of culture duration galactosylation falls by `{python} fx(abs(DUR_GA_LO), 1)` points at the low end of the pH range and by `{python} fx(abs(DUR_GA_HI), 1)` points at the high end. Across the range of pCO2 it falls by `{python} fx(abs(CO2_GA_LO), 1)` and `{python} fx(abs(CO2_GA_HI), 1)` points. Across the range of culture temperature it rises by `{python} fx(TMP_GA_LO, 1)` points at the low end of the pH range and by `{python} fx(TMP_GA_HI, 1)` points at the high end.

High mannose rises with culture pH, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('high_mannose', 'pH'))` across its range, and falls with culture temperature, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('high_mannose', 'temperature'))`. The small interaction of the two is significant. Neither culture duration nor pCO2 is in the model.

Acidic variants fall with pCO2, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('acidic_variants', 'co2'))` across its range, and with culture pH, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('acidic_variants', 'pH'))`. They rise with culture temperature, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('acidic_variants', 'temperature'))`. The main effect of culture duration is a factor of `{python} fx(fold('acidic_variants', 'duration'))` and is not significant (p `{python} pfmt(P_DUR_AC)`). It stays in the model because the interaction of culture pH with culture duration does. The interaction of culture pH with culture temperature is significant. Of the terms of this model, only `{python} term_names(ACID_COMMON)` are carried by every model within `{python} f"{NEAR_D:g}"` AICc units of it (@sec-near), so the other terms are not reported as findings.

Aggregate rises with culture pH, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('aggregates_hmw', 'pH'))` across its range, and with culture duration, by a factor of `{python} fx(fold('aggregates_hmw', 'duration'))`. The interaction of the two is negative on the log scale, so a longer culture multiplies aggregate by less at high pH than at low pH. The squared term of culture pH is negative, so the rise with pH flattens toward the top of the range. Neither culture temperature nor pCO2 is in the model.

@fig-contours shows the response surfaces over culture pH and culture duration, with culture temperature and pCO2 at their set-points. The surfaces are predictions of the scale-down model before the offset, and for a log-scale attribute they show the median.

```{python}
D.fig_rsm_contours(UO)
plt.show()
```

### What the augmentation changed {#sec-augmentation}

The `{python} N_AUG` augmentation runs were added after the results of the planned runs were known, and every selected model is fitted to them. Their pCO2 settings rest on a probe whose calibration status the record does not give (DEV-003-08, equipment not recorded). They changed what the models of this step predict, and with it the headline results.

On the `{python} N_PLAN` planned runs alone, the selected models meet the model F-test, the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting for every attribute. Their NOR-propagated PARs for acidic variants end at pH `{python} APA_TXT['pH'].split('–')[1]` for culture pH, start at `{python} APA_TXT['temperature'].split('–')[0]` °C for culture temperature and end at `{python} APA_TXT['co2'].split('–')[1]` mmHg for pCO2, so none of the three contains the NOR. At the least favourable NOR combination the predicted median is `{python} pct(ALT_PLAN['wc']['predicted'], 2)` and the lower prediction limit `{python} pct(ALT_PLAN['wc']['pi_low'], 2)`, and the design space covers `{python} pct(100 * ALT_PLAN['ds'])` of the region studied. With the plan's full quadratic model on all `{python} N_ALL` runs, the PAR of pCO2 ends at `{python} D._par_str(CO2_FULL).split('–')[1]` mmHg, the design space covers `{python} pct(100 * ALT_FULL['ds'])`, and high mannose exceeds the limit on overfitting. That every PAR contains the NOR, and that the design space covers `{python} pct(100 * DSG['fraction'])`, therefore rests on the augmentation runs and on the model selection together.

A model selected on the same runs on which it is judged passes an optimistic check, and the augmentation runs are an independent one. @tbl-augcheck shows how well the models selected on the planned runs predict the augmentation runs. The models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in POOR])` predict them poorly, with a root mean square error of prediction `{python} fx(AUGC.loc['high_mannose', 'rmsep'] / AUGC.loc['high_mannose', 'rmse_model'], 1)` and `{python} fx(AUGC.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'rmsep'] / AUGC.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'rmse_model'], 1)` times their residual standard deviation. The block term is not significant for any attribute (p ≥ `{python} fx(min(AUGC.block_p), 2)`), so a shift between the two blocks does not explain the misses.

### Near-equivalent models {#sec-near}

Within `{python} f"{NEAR_D:g}"` AICc units of the selected models lie `{python} N_NEAR_OTHERS` other models, `{python} join_and([('none' if NEAR_OTHERS[r] == 0 else str(NEAR_OTHERS[r])) + ' for ' + OUT[r] for r in RESPS])`. Each of them meets the model F-test, the lack-of-fit test and the limit on overfitting, gives the same conclusion over the NOR as the selected model and leaves the scale-down model qualified. They differ from the selected model by `{python} words(min(NEAR_DIFF))` to `{python} words(max(NEAR_DIFF))` terms. For afucosylation some carry `{python} term_names(NEAR['afucosylation']['vary'])`, for high mannose `{python} term_names(NEAR['high_mannose']['vary'])`, and for aggregate `{python} term_names(NEAR['aggregates_hmw']['vary'])`. For acidic variants they share only `{python} term_names(ACID_COMMON)`.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

@tbl-univariate gives every result of the univariate study for the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` attributes, and @tbl-uni-effects the difference between the two ends of each range, both at manufacturing scale. Every result meets its criterion. The half-width of the 95 % confidence interval in @tbl-uni-effects is the precision of each comparison. For galactosylation, for example, a difference smaller than `{python} fx(UV_HW['galactosylation'], 1)` points between the two ends of a range would not have been detected.

The difference is significant at α = `{python} f"{ALPHA:g}"` for a single parameter and attribute. Acidic variants are `{python} fx(UIV_D_MFG)` points higher at the high end of the initial viable cell concentration than at the low end, with a 95 % confidence interval of ± `{python} fx(UIV_HW_MFG)` points (p `{python} pfmt(UIV['p'])`). No effect of dissolved oxygen, basal medium concentration or nutrient feed-1 volume was detected on any attribute, at the precision given in @tbl-uni-effects, and no effect of the initial viable cell concentration was detected on any other attribute.

PCP-003 §6.4 carries a univariate parameter into a multivariate study when it shows an effect on a quality attribute that the mechanism given in PCP-003 §4.3 does not account for. That mechanism, restated in @sec-platform, expects the initial viable cell concentration to change the integral of viable cells and the titre, and no quality attribute. One route to acidic variants would be the time the antibody spends in the culture fluid at culture temperature, since a culture that starts at a higher cell concentration makes its antibody earlier. That route does not account for the effect. Culture duration sets the time in the culture fluid most directly, and it has no detectable main effect on acidic variants, in the screening design (p `{python} pfmt(P_DUR_AC_SCR)`) or in the response-surface model (p `{python} pfmt(P_DUR_AC)`). The parameter should therefore have been carried into a multivariate study and the plan amended. That was not done, and the omission is recorded as the deviation DEV-003-07.

A straight line between the two ends of the range puts acidic variants `{python} fx(abs(IV_NORLO_MFG))` points lower at the NOR low of the initial viable cell concentration than at its set-point, with the other parameters at their set-points. The response-surface and osmolality studies ran at the set-point of this parameter, so the judgement of @sec-criteria-results does not include the effect. Added to the least favourable combination of the `{python} words(len(FS))` response-surface parameters, on the assumption that the effect does not depend on them, it would move the predicted median from `{python} pct(WCA['predicted'], 2)` to `{python} pct(WCA_IV_MED, 2)`, below the lower limit, and the lower prediction limit from `{python} pct(WCA['pi_low'], 2)` to `{python} pct(WCA_IV_LO, 2)`.

## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mechanism}

The fall of galactosylation with culture duration is the direction expected from the depletion of UDP-galactose and of the manganese cofactor of the galactosyltransferase late in the culture (@sec-platform). The fall is much larger at the low end of the pH range than at the high end. Culture pH acts on the same enzyme through the pH of the Golgi, so an interaction was expected, but the study does not show which property of the cell sets its size. Culture temperature raises galactosylation at high pH and has no effect at low pH, and the study does not show why the effect depends on pH.

Afucosylation also falls with culture duration at low pH, and hardly at high pH. The mechanism of @sec-platform predicts the opposite direction. A pool weighted toward antibody made late in the culture, when GDP-fucose and the processing capacity of the Golgi have declined, should carry more antibody without core fucose, not less. The study does not explain the direction.

A higher pCO2 lowers galactosylation, afucosylation and acidic variants. For all three this is the direction of a higher culture pH, while @sec-platform expected a higher pCO2 to act like a lower culture pH, because dissolved carbon dioxide acidifies the cytosol. Osmolality was held constant while pCO2 varied in these designs, so a rise of osmolality does not explain it. The mechanism does not explain the direction of the pCO2 effects.

Acidic variants rise with culture temperature, the direction in which a higher temperature speeds deamidation. They fall as culture pH rises, the opposite of what deamidation alone would give. @sec-platform stated that the net direction of a parameter on acidic variants is not predictable from the chemistry, because sialylation and glycation respond differently, and the study does not identify which route dominates. The effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants is not accounted for by the mechanism either (@sec-univariate).

Aggregate rises with culture pH and with culture duration, the directions expected from the weaker repulsion between antibody molecules as the pH approaches the isoelectric point and from the longer time at temperature (@sec-platform). On the log scale the two effects multiply, so aggregate is highest after a long culture at high pH. High mannose rises with culture pH and falls with culture temperature. A warmer culture speeds the processing enzymes of the Golgi, which is consistent with less high mannose, and the mechanism gives no direction for the pH effect.

For the operation of the step, the attribute nearest its limit is acidic variants at its lower limit. A high culture pH, a high pCO2 and a low culture temperature bring it there, and a high osmolality and a low initial viable cell concentration add to it. Galactosylation approaches its upper limit at low pH, high temperature, short culture and low pCO2, but at the least favourable NOR combination its prediction interval stays `{python} fx(ACC['galactosylation'][1] - WCG['pi_high'], 1)` points below that limit. Routine operation is therefore limited by acidic variants, and the control strategy acts on that corner (@sec-control).

# Design space {#sec-design-space}

The design space of this step is the region of the `{python} words(len(FS))` response-surface parameters over which every modelled attribute meets its intermediate acceptance criterion. It is judged on the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch, as PCMP-001 §6.2 requires. A setting lies inside it when both ends of that interval lie within the criterion of every attribute, at manufacturing scale. Osmolality and the `{python} words(len(UNI))` univariate parameters are held at their set-points, so the design space is conditioned on them, and it is not claimed beyond the ranges studied.

On the grid of `{python} f"{DSG['n_points']:,}"` points, `{python} pct(100 * DSG['fraction'])` of the region studied lies inside the design space. Acidic variants decide its boundary. They exclude `{python} pct(100 * DSG['per_response']['acidic_variants'])` of the grid points, galactosylation `{python} pct(100 * DSG['per_response']['galactosylation'])` and afucosylation `{python} pct(100 * DSG['per_response']['afucosylation'])`, and high mannose and aggregate exclude none. On the mean prediction in place of the single-batch interval, `{python} pct(100 * DSM['fraction'])` of the grid would lie inside. A region drawn on mean predictions gives a single batch at its edge only about an even chance of meeting the criterion [@amab2009], so it is shown here for comparison only. On the planned runs alone the design space would cover `{python} pct(100 * ALT_PLAN['ds'])` (@sec-augmentation).

@fig-design-space shows two planes of the design space in culture pH and pCO2, evaluated on a grid of `{python} DS_PG_N` by `{python} DS_PG_N` settings within the NOR of the two parameters. In the first, culture temperature and culture duration are at their set-points, and `{python} pct(100 * DS_SHARE[0])` of that grid, at the corner of high pH and high pCO2, lies outside the design space. In the second, culture temperature is at its NOR low and culture duration at its NOR high, the settings least favourable for acidic variants, and `{python} pct(100 * DS_SHARE[1])` lies outside. The NOR therefore does not lie entirely inside the design space, and @sec-criteria-results gives the decision not to narrow it (DEV-003-04).

```{python}
#| label: fig-design-space
#| fig-cap: "Two planes of the design space in culture pH and pCO2, on the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch at manufacturing scale. Left, culture temperature and culture duration at their set-points. Right, culture temperature at its NOR low and culture duration at its NOR high. Plain green, every attribute meets its criterion. Hatched red, at least one does not. The rectangle is the NOR and the cross the set-point."
fig_design_space()
plt.show()
```

The design space is not the product of the PARs of @sec-par-table. Each PAR holds while the other parameters vary about their set-points, and the design space must hold at every combination of settings at once. As ICH Q8(R2) states, working within the design space is not considered a change from a regulatory filing perspective [@ichq8]. Movement within it is still assessed under the change management of the quality system, and a move outside it is a change [@ichq10]. The design space rests on the scale-down model and is not confirmed at commercial scale at its edges.

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-par}

## Acceptance criteria {#sec-criteria}

Each output is judged against its intermediate acceptance criterion (@tbl-iac). PCMP-001 §7.3 derives the criterion from the drug substance criterion by carrying it backward through the worst case of every downstream step on the platform, with no margin. Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose keep their drug substance criteria, because no downstream step changes them. The upper limit of acidic variants is carried back through the platform worst case of the increase across low-pH viral inactivation, `{python} fx(float(vi_acid.assumed))` points, to `{python} pct(ACC['acidic_variants'][1])`. In the low-pH response-surface design every run at the same hold time gave the same acidic-variant result, so the full quadratic model reproduces the results exactly, cannot be judged against PCMP-001 §7.2, and the platform value stands. The lower limit is carried back unchanged, which assumes that no downstream step lowers acidic variants (PCP-003 §12).

The aggregate criterion is the drug substance limit multiplied by the aggregate clearance factor of cation exchange, less the aggregate increase across low-pH viral inactivation. From the platform values alone it is `{python} pct(AGG.iac_high_apriori, 2)`. Verification of the platform worst cases changed both terms (PCMP-001 §7.5). The cation exchange model predicted within its NOR a lowest clearance of `{python} fx(float(cex_agg.predicted_nor))`-fold, worse than the platform worst case of `{python} fx(float(cex_agg.assumed))`-fold. The one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single batch there, `{python} fx(float(cex_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))`-fold, replaced the platform value (PCR-007), which alone would set the criterion at `{python} pct(AGG_TIGHT_ONLY, 2)`. The low-pH viral inactivation model gave a bound of `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))` points for the increase, better than the platform value of `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.assumed))` points, on a model that meets the first three adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 (PCR-006). That bound replaced the platform value too. The criterion in force is `{python} pct(AGG.iac_high, 2)`, stricter than the a priori value.

PCMP-001 §7.5 asks for the risk of the change. The net change is a tightening, so more batches would fail at this step and fewer would reach the patient with too much aggregate, and the risk moves toward the producer. The widening alone moves the criterion `{python} fx(AGG.iac_high - AGG_TIGHT_ONLY)` points back toward the patient. This report sets no in-process test of aggregate at harvest, so an excursion beyond the criterion would be detected at release, where aggregate is tested by SEC against the drug substance limit of `{python} pct(DS_AGG, 1)`. To meet that limit, cation exchange must clear at least `{python} fx(float(cex_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))`-fold and low-pH viral inactivation must add no more than `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.predicted_nor_bound95))` points. At the highest single-batch level that the model of this step predicts within the NOR, `{python} pct(AGG_UP, 2)` at manufacturing scale, the drug substance would then carry at most `{python} pct(DS_AGG_EST, 2)`. None of the `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` batches of the integrated model fell outside the aggregate criterion of the drug substance, which puts the probability below `{python} pct(100 * P_UB0, 2)` at one-sided 95 % confidence (@sec-capability).

The widening rests on the bound of the low-pH viral inactivation model, from the `{python} N_VI_RSM` runs of its response-surface design. That model has predicted R² `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.r2_minus_pred_r2), 3)` below R² and a lack-of-fit p-value of `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.p_lack_of_fit), 3)`, and it also meets the criterion on residuals and influential runs. PCR-006 gives the bound and states whether it depends on a single run, as PCMP-001 §7.5 requires. The platform worst case is an increase over a hold of `{python} f"{VIH.prange[1]:g}"` min, while the NOR of the A-Mab hold as characterized ends at `{python} f"{VIH_MAX:g}"` min. At the edges of the range studied, which include the longer hold, A-Mab added up to `{python} fx(float(vi_agg.observed_edge))` points, more than the platform value. The replacement therefore reflects the shorter hold of A-Mab and not a more stable product. It holds for routine manufacture, which is controlled within the hold-time NOR, and the NOR of hold time and temperature in force ends at the same longest hold and highest temperature as the NOR as characterized.

Without the model selection of INV-002 corrective action CA3, the verification would have used the full quadratic models. The aggregate criterion would then be `{python} pct(ACC_WO['aggregates_hmw'][1], 2)` and the upper limit of acidic variants `{python} pct(ACC_WO['acidic_variants'][1], 1)`. Judged against those criteria with the models of this report, no conclusion over the NOR, no PAR and no qualification of the scale-down model changes.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.iac_derivation(["bioreactor"]).show()
```

## Outputs against their criteria over the NOR {#sec-criteria-results}

@tbl-criteria-bioreactor gives each output against its criterion, with the mean predicted at the set-point and its range over the NOR. The verdict is judged on the prediction interval of a single batch at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high. Afucosylation, galactosylation, high mannose and aggregate meet their criteria. Acidic variants do not. At `{python} words(N_FAIL_COMB)` of the `{python} N_NORCOMB` combinations, all with pCO2 at its NOR high, the lower end of the prediction interval falls below `{python} pct(ACC['acidic_variants'][0])`. The least favourable combination is culture pH at its NOR high, culture temperature at its NOR low, culture duration at its NOR high and pCO2 at its NOR high. There the predicted median at manufacturing scale is `{python} pct(WCA['predicted'], 2)`, above the lower limit, and the prediction interval runs from `{python} pct(WCA['pi_low'], 2)` to `{python} pct(WCA['pi_high'], 2)`. With the initial viable cell concentration at its NOR low the median would fall to about `{python} pct(WCA_IV_MED, 2)` (@sec-univariate). The upper limit is met at every combination. The conclusion holds with the offset at either end of its interval (@sec-sdm).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.criteria_results("bioreactor").show()
```

PCP-003 §7 requires the NOR to lie inside the declared operating region, and the NOR to be narrowed until it does. The NOR was not narrowed (DEV-003-04). Every combination that fails has pCO2 at its NOR high, so the NOR of pCO2 is the one whose narrowing would act on all of them. Some fail with culture pH at its set-point, so narrowing the NOR of culture pH alone would not restore the criterion. A NOR is the range in which the process is routinely controlled, and narrowing it was judged impractical. The risk was accepted on the following grounds.

1. Acidic variants have very low criticality, and their lower limit of `{python} pct(ACC['acidic_variants'][0])` was set from the range of results seen with the product.
2. On all `{python} N_ALL` runs the NOR-propagated PARs contain the NOR, with a margin of `{python} fx(MARG_SD['pH'])` standard deviations of routine variation in culture pH and `{python} fx(MARG_SD['co2'])` in pCO2 (@sec-par-table). The containment rests on the `{python} N_AUG` augmentation runs, added after the planned results were known and set with a pCO2 probe whose calibration is not recorded (DEV-003-08), and on the model selection. On the `{python} N_PLAN` planned runs alone the PARs of culture pH, culture temperature and pCO2 for acidic variants do not contain the NOR (@sec-augmentation). This ground therefore does not support the decision on its own.
3. A batch below the limit is detected by the release test of the drug substance against the acidic-variant criterion and does not reach the patient, so the risk of a failure falls on the producer.
4. In the integrated model of the train, `{python} words(int(PO.loc['acidic_variants', 'n_oos']))` of the `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` simulated batches fell outside the acidic-variant criterion (@sec-capability). That model carries no effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants.

With osmolality at its NOR high the mean of acidic variants at the least favourable combination falls below the lower limit as well (@sec-osmolality). The same decision accepts that case and adds an alarm inside the osmolality NOR on its upper side. The mitigation is the monitoring of acidic variants at harvest and alarm limits inside the NOR, on the side that lowers acidic variants, for culture pH, pCO2 and osmolality (@sec-control). The effect of the initial viable cell concentration is not part of this decision.

## PARs {#sec-par-table}

A PAR is a range of a parameter within which the attribute is shown by supportive data to remain acceptable. ICH Q8(R2) defines it with the other parameters kept constant [@ichq8], which is the set-point analysis. The NOR-propagated analysis lets the other parameters vary across their NORs and judges a single batch, so it is stricter, and it is the PAR that supports a claim (PCMP-001 §6.4). @tbl-par gives both for each of the `{python} words(len(FS))` response-surface parameters and each of the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` attributes, from the selected model of the attribute with the offset applied. Objective 3 requires a PAR where the selected model has a significant term in the parameter, `{python} N_SIGT` of the `{python} N_PAR` combinations. The other `{python} words(N_PAR - N_SIGT)`, `{python} NOSIG_TXT`, have no term in the parameter and are given for information.

Every NOR-propagated PAR contains the NOR, and `{python} N_PAR - len(NARROW)` span the whole range studied. The exceptions are the PARs of culture pH and pCO2 for acidic variants. The PAR of culture pH ends `{python} fx(PMA.loc['pH', 'nor_hi'], 3)` pH units above the NOR high, and the PAR of pCO2 ends `{python} pv('co2', PMA.loc['co2', 'nor_hi'])` above it. Measured in standard deviations of the routine variation of each parameter, the width of its NOR divided by `{python} f"{D.NOR_SD_DIVISOR:g}"` (PCMP-001 §6.4), the margin is `{python} fx(MARG_SD['pH'])` for culture pH and `{python} fx(MARG_SD['co2'])` for pCO2. On the planned runs alone these two PARs and that of culture temperature do not contain the NOR (@sec-augmentation). In the set-point analysis every PAR spans the range studied.

The range carried into the control strategy for each parameter is the intersection of its required PARs (PCP-003 §7, PCMP-001 §7.6). It is pH `{python} INT_TXT['pH']` for culture pH, `{python} INT_TXT['temperature']` °C for culture temperature, `{python} INT_TXT['duration']` days for culture duration and `{python} INT_TXT['co2']` mmHg for pCO2.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rk = {D.RESP_LABEL[_r]: _r for _r in RESPS}
_fk = {PRM[_f].name: _f for _f in FS}
_pt = PT.drop(columns=["Basis", "Char. range"]).copy()
_pt.insert(4, "NOR", [nor_txt(_fk[p_]).replace("pH ", "") if PRM[_fk[p_]].unit == "pH" else f"{PRM[_fk[p_]].nor[0]:g}–{PRM[_fk[p_]].nor[1]:g}"
                      for p_ in _pt["Parameter"]])
_pt.insert(5, "Required", ["yes" if SIGT[(_rk[c_], _fk[p_])] else "no" for c_, p_ in zip(_pt["CQA"], _pt["Parameter"])])
_pt["CQA"] = _pt["CQA"].map({D.RESP_LABEL[_r]: ANAME[_r] for _r in RESPS})
_pt = _pt[["CQA", "Criterion", "Parameter", "Unit", "NOR", "Required", "PAR (set-point)", "PAR (NOR)"]]
T.frame(_pt, "Proven acceptable ranges of the response-surface parameters for each attribute, at manufacturing "
        "scale.", "tbl-par", merge=["CQA", "Criterion"],
        header={"CQA": "Attribute", "PAR (set-point)": "PAR, others\nat set-point", "PAR (NOR)": "PAR, others\nacross NOR",
                "Required": "Required by\nobjective 3"},
        align=["P{3.0cm}", "l", "P{3.4cm}", "l", "l", "l", "l", "l"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Every PAR is computed from the selected model of the attribute. PAR, others at set-point: the mean "
                    "prediction with the other factors at their set-points. PAR, others across NOR: the 95 % interval of a "
                    "single batch with the other factors drawn across their NORs, the PAR that supports a claim. Required "

                    "toward the inside of the range, to three significant figures. The range studied of each parameter "
                    "is given in the table of process parameters.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The PAR of pCO2 is a range at the set-point of osmolality, because the response-surface model holds osmolality there. At manufacturing scale a higher pCO2 raises the osmolality as bicarbonate accumulates, and a higher osmolality lowers acidic variants (@sec-osmolality). The PAR of pCO2 for acidic variants therefore does not include the effect of the osmolality rise that comes with it at scale.

@fig-par-afucosylation to @fig-par-aggregates show, for each attribute, the PAR of the parameter with the largest main effect in its selected model. The acceptable region is shaded green, the NOR grey and the criterion dashed. The left panel is the set-point analysis and the right panel the NOR-propagated analysis, with the median and the 95 % interval of a single batch. Values are at manufacturing scale.

## Univariate parameters and osmolality {#sec-par-uni}

The ranges of the `{python} words(len(UNI))` univariate parameters are supported by their own data, with the other parameters at their set-points (PCMP-001 §4). Every result met its criterion at both ends of each range (@tbl-univariate), so the range studied of each parameter is supported for the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` attributes at that condition. For the initial viable cell concentration the support does not extend to the other parameters at their least favourable NOR settings for acidic variants (@sec-univariate). Osmolality has no PAR from a model, because it was not a factor of the response-surface design. The osmolality study supports its NOR for every attribute except acidic variants, at the single combination of the other parameters that it tested, and no range of osmolality beyond its NOR is claimed.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

@tbl-capability gives the capability of the drug substance for the `{python} words(len(KEYS))` attributes that this step sets, from the `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` simulated batches of the integrated model. Each Cpk is judged against the target of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` and the minimum of `{python} fx(CPK_MIN)` of PCMP-001 §7.9. A Cpk between the two is acceptable, and a Cpk below the minimum needs an action in the control strategy.

The integrated model simulates manufacturing-scale batches through the whole train. It does not use the response-surface models of this report, and it applies no scale-down offset, because it simulates manufacturing scale directly. Its drug substance means differ from the predictions of @tbl-criteria-bioreactor, for afucosylation `{python} pct(MC_MEAN['afucosylation'], 2)` against `{python} pct(SP_MFG['afucosylation'], 2)` predicted at the set-point. It draws every parameter of the step as the NOR-propagated analysis does, including osmolality, which acts on acidic variants in the integrated model. It carries no effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants, so the capability does not include the effect found in the univariate study (DEV-003-07).

```{python}
#| output: asis
_rows = []
for _k in KEYS:
    _c, _po = CAPT.loc[_k], PO.loc[_k]
    _cr = f"≤ {_c['acc_high']:g}" if _c["spec_type"] == "upper" else f"{_c['acc_low']:g}–{_c['acc_high']:g}"
    _v = ("above the target" if _c["Cpk"] >= CPK_TARGET else
          "between the minimum and the target" if _c["Cpk"] >= CPK_MIN else "below the minimum")
    _f3 = lambda v: T.num(v) if abs(v) >= 0.01 else (f"{v:.{1 - int(math.floor(math.log10(abs(v))))}f}" if v else "0")
    _mean, _sd = (DNA_MC_MEAN, DNA_MC_SD) if _k == "residual_dna" else (_c["mean"], _c["sd"])
    _rows.append([ANAME[_k], CRL[_k], _cr, _f3(_mean), _f3(_sd), f"{_c['Cpk']:.2f}", _v,
                  str(int(_po["n_oos"])), f"{_po['ppm_normal']:.3g}"])
_cp = pd.DataFrame(_rows, columns=["Attribute", "Criticality", "Criterion", "Mean", "SD", "Cpk", "Against PCMP-001",
                                   "Batches outside", "Normal tail (per million)"])
T.frame(_cp, f"Capability of the drug substance for the attributes that the production bioreactor sets, from "
        f"{N_MC:,} batches of the integrated model.", "tbl-capability",
        header={"Criticality": "Criti-\ncality", "Against PCMP-001": "Against the target\nand minimum",
                "Batches outside": "Batches\noutside", "Normal tail (per million)": "Normal tail\n(per million)"},
        align=["P{3.2cm}", "l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "P{3.0cm}", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", f"Cpk is the lower of the two one-sided indices for a two-sided criterion. Batches outside, of {N_MC:,}. "
                    "Normal tail, the tail probability of a normal distribution with the simulated mean and standard "
                    "deviation. Residual DNA per dose for the dose in the text.")], notes_per_row=True).show()
```

The Cpk of acidic variants is `{python} fx(ACAP.Cpk)`, between the minimum and the target, and it is limited by the lower limit, with an index of `{python} fx(ACAP.Cpl)` for the lower limit and `{python} fx(ACAP.Cpu)` for the upper. A higher pCO2, a higher culture pH and a lower culture temperature move acidic variants toward the lower limit (@sec-effects), and so does a higher osmolality (@sec-osmolality). In the simulation `{python} words(int(PO.loc['acidic_variants', 'n_oos']))` of the `{python} f"{N_MC:,}"` batches fell outside the criterion, and the normal tail probability is `{python} f"{PO.loc['acidic_variants', 'ppm_normal']:.0f}"` per million. PCMR-001 consolidates this capability with the risk decision of @sec-criteria-results.

Every other attribute that the step sets has a Cpk above the target, and none of the simulated batches fell outside its criterion. With no simulated batch outside, the probability of a batch outside is below `{python} pct(100 * P_UB0, 2)` at one-sided 95 % confidence. That bound covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the integrated model. Aggregate in the drug substance lies far below its limit, at a mean of `{python} pct(CAPT.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'mean'], 2)`, so its Cpk of `{python} fx(CAPT.loc['aggregates_hmw', 'Cpk'], 1)` mainly reflects that distance. Aggregate is judged instead on the prediction interval of a single batch over the NOR of this step (@sec-criteria-results) and of the steps after it.

Host cell protein and residual DNA in the drug substance depend on the clearance of the downstream steps, which the integrated model takes from Protein A, cation exchange and anion exchange (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008). This step contributes the load, which @sec-sampling gives for information. Residual DNA is judged in ng per dose, for the weekly dose of `{python} f"{DOSE_MGKG:g}"` mg/kg of the A-Mab case study and a body weight of `{python} f"{DOSE_KG:g}"` kg. The body weight is an assumption of this campaign.

# Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

The parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7 [@amab2009]. A parameter whose variation affects a critical quality attribute within the range studied is a CPP when it has a high risk of falling outside its acceptable range in operation. It is a WC-CPP when that risk is low, because the parameter is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR. A parameter that affects process performance and no critical quality attribute is a KPP. A parameter with no relevant effect on either is a GPP. Neither PCMP-001 nor SOP-4001 sets a numerical threshold for a relevant effect or a wide PAR, so each class below is argued from the effect sizes of @tbl-effect-size and from the margin between each PAR and its NOR.

- Culture pH is a WC-CPP. It changes all `{python} words(len(CRIT_K))` critical attributes, and its effect on high mannose is large. Its NOR-propagated PARs for the critical attributes span the range studied, and its PAR for acidic variants ends `{python} fx(MARG_SD['pH'])` routine standard deviations above the NOR high. It is readily controlled by carbon dioxide and base addition.
- Culture temperature is a WC-CPP. Its effects on afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose are moderate, and its NOR-propagated PARs span the range studied for every attribute. It is readily controlled by the vessel jacket.
- pCO2 is a WC-CPP. Its effect on galactosylation is moderate and on afucosylation small, and its NOR-propagated PARs for these attributes span the range studied. Its PAR for acidic variants ends `{python} fx(MARG_SD['co2'])` routine standard deviations above the NOR high. It is controlled by the sparge.
- Osmolality is a WC-CPP. The screening showed it lowering galactosylation by `{python} fx(abs(eff('galactosylation', OSM_L)))` points across its range, and the osmolality study showed it lowering afucosylation by `{python} fx(abs(OSM_CH['afucosylation']))` points across its NOR. It has no PAR from a model, so the wide PAR that PCMP-001 §7.7 names for a WC-CPP cannot be shown for it, and at its NOR high acidic variants fall below their limit at the least favourable combination of the other parameters (@sec-osmolality). It is controlled through the base and feed additions.
- Culture duration is a WC-CPP. Its effects on galactosylation and afucosylation are large and on aggregate moderate, and its NOR-propagated PARs span the range studied for every attribute. It is set by the day of harvest.
- Dissolved oxygen is a KPP. No effect was detected on any attribute measured, at the precision of @tbl-uni-effects. The record holds no growth or titre result (DEV-003-05). @sec-platform expects the culture not to be limited by oxygen across the range studied, which points to no effect on process performance either. The expectation and the class conflict, and the data of this study cannot resolve it.
- The initial viable cell concentration is a KPP. It raises acidic variants, an attribute of very low criticality, by `{python} fx(UIV_D_MFG)` points across its range, and no effect on a critical attribute was detected. The class rests on its role in growth and titre (@sec-platform), which the record does not hold. Its effect on acidic variants calls for the multivariate study recorded as DEV-003-07.
- Basal medium concentration is a GPP. No effect was detected on any attribute measured, and the record holds no growth or titre result. PCP-003 §4.1 expects a higher basal medium concentration to raise growth and titre, which under PCMP-001 §7.7 points to a KPP. The expectation and the class conflict, and the data of this study cannot resolve it.
- Nutrient feed-1 volume is a KPP. No effect was detected on any attribute measured. The class rests on its role in the supply of glucose, amino acids and precursors for growth and titre (@sec-platform), which the record does not hold. The feed under-delivery of DEV-003-02 left the feed within its NOR (@sec-dev-02).

The step has `{python} words(NCLS['WC-CPP'])` well-controlled critical process parameters, `{python} words(NCLS['KPP'])` KPPs and `{python} words(NCLS['GPP'])` GPP.

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-control}

This step contributes the following elements to the control strategy of A-Mab.

1. The `{python} words(NCLS['WC-CPP'])` WC-CPPs are held within their NORs by the bioreactor control system. Culture pH is controlled by carbon dioxide and base addition, culture temperature by the vessel jacket, pCO2 by the sparge, osmolality through the base and feed additions, and culture duration by the day of harvest. The ranges carried into the control strategy are those of @sec-par-table.
2. Alarm limits inside the NOR are set on the side that lowers acidic variants, the upper side for culture pH, for pCO2 and for osmolality. Their values are not in the record of this step.
3. Acidic variants are measured at harvest. The measurement detects a low result before purification, but it cannot change the batch, and the record of this step gives no action limit for it.
4. The KPPs are held within their NORs for process consistency. The delivered feed is checked by the mass reconciliation after the run, which detected DEV-003-02. The basal medium is prepared at its set-point under SOP-2004.
5. The drug substance criteria of the attributes this step sets apply at release (PCMP-001 §3). The glycans, acidic variants and aggregate are tested there by the methods of @sec-analytical.
6. The host cell protein that this step releases into the harvest is cleared by Protein A, cation exchange and anion exchange, and is judged at each of those steps and at the drug substance. Residual DNA is cleared by the same steps and judged at the drug substance only (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008).
7. Process performance qualification (PPQ) at the receiving site under PTP-001 runs the process at its set-points. It confirms the process at scale near the centre of the NOR and does not test the edges of the ranges.

PCMR-001 consolidates these elements with those of the other steps into the control strategy of the whole process.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The conclusions of this report rest on the scale-down model, whose offsets are known well enough that no conclusion over the NOR depends on their exact size. Four facts limit how far that holds. The offset was estimated at the set-points only, so its use toward the edges of the range studied is an assumption. The carbon dioxide stripping of the commercial vessel was not matched, and osmolality was set independently of pCO2 (@sec-operation). The growth and titre of the runs are not in the record, so the model cannot be compared with manufacturing scale on process performance (DEV-003-05). The difference in aggregate between the scales has no known cause (DEV-003-09).

The following limitations apply to the conclusions of this report.

1. The containment of the NOR by every PAR, and the size of the design space, rest on the `{python} N_AUG` augmentation runs, added after the planned results were known, and on the model selection. On the planned runs alone three PARs for acidic variants do not contain the NOR.
2. The models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in RI_FAIL])` do not meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs, because their residual spread grows with the predicted value. With that growth allowed for, the judgement over the NOR is the same.
3. For acidic variants, `{python} NEAR_OTHERS['acidic_variants']` other models lie within `{python} f"{NEAR_D:g}"` AICc units of the selected one and only `{python} term_names(ACID_COMMON)` are common to all of them. The conclusion over the NOR is the same for each, but the other terms are not findings. At the set-point the model of acidic variants predicts above the mean of the centre points (@sec-models).
4. Osmolality has no PAR from a model, and its interactions with the other parameters are known only from the screening design (DEV-003-03).
5. The effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants comes from a univariate study, which cannot show its interactions, and the multivariate study that PCP-003 §6.4 requires has not been made (DEV-003-07). The capability does not include it.
6. The pCO2 settings of the augmentation and osmolality studies rest on equipment whose calibration status is not recorded (DEV-003-08).
7. The directions of the pCO2 effects and of the effect of culture duration on afucosylation are not the ones the mechanism of @sec-platform gives, and the study does not explain them.
8. The design space is not confirmed at commercial scale at its edges, and the capability comes from the integrated model, not from the models of this report.

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. The relationship of each parameter with each attribute was quantified (objective 1). The selected response-surface models describe the `{python} words(len(RESPS))` attributes over the ranges studied, and culture pH interacts with most of the other parameters.
2. The multivariate region was defined on the 95 % prediction interval of a single batch (objective 2). It covers `{python} pct(100 * DSG['fraction'])` of the region studied, `{python} pct(100 * ALT_PLAN['ds'])` on the planned runs alone, and acidic variants decide its boundary. The NOR does not lie entirely inside it (DEV-003-04).
3. A PAR was established for each response-surface parameter and each attribute whose selected model has a significant term in it, `{python} N_SIGT` in all (objective 3). On all runs every PAR contains the NOR, a result that rests on the augmentation runs and the model selection. Osmolality has no PAR from a model.
4. Each parameter was classified (objective 4). The step has `{python} words(NCLS['WC-CPP'])` WC-CPPs, `{python} words(NCLS['KPP'])` KPPs and `{python} words(NCLS['GPP'])` GPP. The classes of dissolved oxygen, basal medium concentration and osmolality are not fully supported by the evidence of this study (@sec-classification).
5. The capability supports the control strategy of @sec-control (objective 5). The lowest Cpk of the drug substance is that of acidic variants, `{python} fx(ACAP.Cpk)`, between the minimum and the target of PCMP-001, and every other attribute that the step sets has a Cpk above the target.
6. The scale-down model is qualified for every output with a criterion.
7. Against the completion criteria of PCP-003 §7, the study is complete except for the operating region, which does not contain the NOR for acidic variants (DEV-003-04), for osmolality, which has no PAR from a model (DEV-003-03), and for the multivariate study of the initial viable cell concentration (DEV-003-07).
8. The results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Deviations and discrepancies from the plan {#sec-deviations}

A deviation is a departure from an approved procedure or a rule of the approved plan, or an unplanned event in the execution. A discrepancy from the plan is work that the plan did not foresee, with no such departure. @tbl-dev-register lists the `{python} words(N_DEV)` deviations of this step, and @tbl-disc-register the `{python} words(N_PD)` discrepancies from PCP-003.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Deviations recorded for the production bioreactor studies. {#tbl-dev-register}")
```

## DEV-003-01, pCO2 probe drift during screening run 4 {#sec-dev-01}

During screening run 4 the pCO2 probe of the scale-down system, EQ-BRX-205, read `{python} pv('co2', DRIFT)` higher than the offline reference, and the comparison of the two in in-process monitoring detected the drift. The controller held the probe reading at the design level of `{python} pv('co2', R4_CO2)`, so the run ran at about `{python} pv('co2', R4_REC)`. The record gives the cause as drift of the probe between two calibrations, and the equipment record shows the probe in calibration at the time of execution.

The run is analysed at its recorded setting, a shift of `{python} fx(abs(DRIFT_CODED), 3)` in coded units, in which 1 is the half-range of pCO2. With the run at its design setting instead, the set of significant effects is the same for every attribute. The residual of run 4 on the screening model is at most `{python} fx(R4_MAXZ)` times the residual standard deviation for any attribute. With run 4 excluded the screening model keeps `{python} words(R4['afucosylation']['excl_df'])` residual degrees of freedom. Fewer effects then reach significance for `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in R4_FEWER])`, and for afucosylation the same number, but not the same set. The run was retained. The record names screening run 4 only. The response-surface design ran later on the same probe, and the record shows no recalibration between the two designs, so it does not show whether the probe read high in those runs too.

## DEV-003-02, nutrient feed-1 under-delivery on a centre-point batch {#sec-dev-02}

A centre-point batch of the screening design received `{python} pct(float(dev_003_02_feed_deficit_pct))` less nutrient feed-1 than its target, from lot LOT-FED-3120. The mass reconciliation after the run detected it, and its cause was a calibration offset of the feed pump. The batch received a feed volume of about `{python} pv('feed_vol', FEED_DELIV, 1)`, inside the NOR of `{python} nor_txt('feed_vol')` and the range studied of `{python} range_txt('feed_vol')`, and the univariate study detected no effect of the nutrient feed-1 volume on any attribute across that range (@sec-univariate). The glycan results of the batch were confirmed by `{python} words(int(dev_003_02_ver_n))` determinations by the glycan map (SOP-3010, validated under AMV-3010). With the precision of the method, `{python} words(int(dev_003_02_ver_n))` determinations give a 95 % confidence interval of ± `{python} pct(float(dev_003_02_ci_hw), 2)` of the result. The deviation and lot records name the batch as a screening centre point but not its run number, and @tbl-centre gives the spread of the `{python} words(NC_SCR)` centre points. The batch was retained.

## DEV-003-03, osmolality not carried into the response-surface design {#sec-dev-03}

The screening showed osmolality active on acidic variants and on galactosylation (@sec-screening). PCP-003 §6.3 requires the factors carried into the response-surface design to be those that the screening identifies as active, with the design amended before execution if they differ from the planned subset. Osmolality was not carried forward and the design was not amended. The departure was found in the Version 2.0 re-analysis of the screening results. Osmolality had been left out because its range studied is the narrowest relative to its NOR, against the rule of the plan. Every prediction, PAR and the design space of this report are therefore conditioned on osmolality at its set-point. The osmolality study measured the effect of osmolality at the combination of NOR settings least favourable for acidic variants (PD-003-01, @sec-osmolality), and its interactions with the other parameters are known from the screening design only.

## DEV-003-04, NOR not narrowed for acidic variants {#sec-dev-04}

Acidic variants do not meet their criterion over the NOR on the prediction interval of a single batch (@sec-criteria-results), and the NOR was not narrowed as PCP-003 §7 requires. The departure was found in the Version 2.0 re-analysis against the criteria of PCMP-001 Version 2.0. The narrowing rule was set aside by a risk decision, whose grounds and mitigation @sec-criteria-results gives.

## DEV-003-05, process outputs not in the study record {#sec-dev-05}

The viable cell density, the viability and the titre of the qualification and characterization runs are not in the study record. PCP-003 §5.4 requires the culture to be monitored for viable cell density and viability, and §5.1 lists both, with the titre, among the outputs of the qualification. The review of the study record against PCP-003 found the gap. The monitoring records were kept in the scale-down system and were not transferred to the study record, and they cannot be recovered. No criterion of this report depends on these outputs. Their absence means that the classes of the KPPs and the GPP rest on platform knowledge for process performance (@sec-classification), and that the scale-down model was not compared with manufacturing scale on growth and titre.

## DEV-003-06, univariate study started before the response-surface study {#sec-dev-06}

The univariate study started on `{python} S0('S-BRX-UNI')`, before the response-surface study started on `{python} S0('S-BRX-RSM')`. PCP-003 §11 places the univariate assessments after the response-surface design. The departure was found in the review of the execution dates (INV-001 finding 5), and its cause was the scheduling of the bioreactors. The sequence exists so that the factors of the response-surface design are chosen from the screening result. The screening study had ended on `{python} S1('S-BRX-SCR')`, before either study started, and the univariate parameters were assigned by RA-001 and were not candidates for the response-surface design. The order of the two studies therefore affects no analysis, and the data were retained.

## DEV-003-07, initial viable cell concentration not carried into a multivariate study {#sec-dev-07}

The univariate study showed acidic variants `{python} fx(UIV_D_MFG)` points higher at the high end of the initial viable cell concentration than at the low end, at manufacturing scale (@sec-univariate). The mechanism of PCP-003 §4.3 does not account for the effect, so PCP-003 §6.4 carries the parameter into a multivariate study and amends the plan. That was not done, because the univariate results were not analysed for this rule in Version 1.0. The departure was found in the Version 2.0 re-analysis of the univariate results. With the parameter at its NOR low and the other parameters at their least favourable NOR combination, the effect would take the predicted median of acidic variants to about `{python} pct(WCA_IV_MED, 2)`, below the lower limit, and the lower prediction limit to `{python} pct(WCA_IV_LO, 2)` (@sec-univariate). The judgement over the NOR and the capability of this report do not include the effect.

## DEV-003-08, equipment and calibration status not recorded for two studies {#sec-dev-08}

The records of the osmolality study S-BRX-OSM and the augmentation S-BRX-AUG name no equipment and state no calibration status of the pCO2 probe, which PCP-003 §9 and preventive action PA3 of INV-001 require. The review of the study record found the gap, and the records cannot be completed. If the studies used EQ-BRX-205, its next calibration was due on `{python} PROBE_DUE`, before both studies started. pCO2 varied from `{python} pv('co2', PRM['co2'].prange[0])` to `{python} pv('co2', PRM['co2'].prange[1])` in the `{python} N_AUG` augmentation runs and was held at `{python} pv('co2', WCA['settings']['co2'])` in the osmolality study, so the accuracy of those settings is not documented. A probe that read high, as in DEV-003-01, would put the true pCO2 below the recorded level. Every selected model is fitted to the augmentation runs, and the containment of the NOR by the PARs rests on them (@sec-augmentation).

## DEV-003-09, aggregate difference between the scales not investigated {#sec-dev-09}

PCP-003 Version 1.0 accepted the scale-down model for an output only where the two scales showed no statistically significant difference at p < 0.05, and required a difference to be investigated before the characterization runs. For aggregate the qualification shows such a difference (p `{python} pfmt(V1T['aggregates_hmw'])`), and no investigation was made before the screening study started. The re-analysis of the qualification against the Version 1.0 rule found it. Under PCMP-001 Version 2.0 aggregate is judged through its offset, a ratio of `{python} fx(SDM['aggregates_hmw']['offset'], 3)` with a `{python} OFF_CI` % confidence interval of `{python} fx(SDM['aggregates_hmw']['lo'], 3)` to `{python} fx(SDM['aggregates_hmw']['hi'], 3)`, and the model is qualified for it (@tbl-sdm-offsets). The cause of the difference is not known.

## PD-003-01, osmolality study {#sec-pd-01}

The osmolality study (@sec-osm-design) showed that osmolality at its NOR high takes the mean of acidic variants at the least favourable NOR combination below the lower limit, which added an osmolality alarm to the mitigation of @sec-criteria-results. It also showed that a higher osmolality lowers afucosylation (@sec-osmolality).

## PD-003-02, augmentation of the response-surface design {#sec-pd-02}

PCP-003 planned the `{python} N_PLAN` runs of the face-centred design. The `{python} N_AUG` runs added under INV-002 changed the selected models of `{python} words(len(AUG_CHANGED))` attributes, and the models selected on the planned runs predict them poorly for high mannose and aggregate. With the selected models on the planned runs alone, the PARs of culture pH, culture temperature and pCO2 for acidic variants would not contain the NOR, and the design space would cover `{python} pct(100 * ALT_PLAN['ds'])` instead of `{python} pct(100 * DSG['fraction'])` (@sec-augmentation). The full quadratic model of high mannose still exceeds the limit on overfitting on all runs.

## PD-003-03, model selection {#sec-pd-03}

With the plan's full quadratic model in place of the selected models, on all `{python} N_ALL` runs, high mannose would have no adequate model, the PAR of pCO2 for acidic variants would end at `{python} D._par_str(CO2_FULL).split('–')[1]` mmHg, inside the NOR, and the design space would cover `{python} pct(100 * ALT_FULL['ds'])`. The selection also changes the criteria of this step through the verification of the downstream steps (@sec-criteria).

## PD-003-04, models that do not meet the criterion on residuals and influential runs {#sec-pd-04}

The selected models of `{python} join_and([OUT[r] for r in RI_FAIL])` were used although the spread of their residuals grows with the predicted value. No run of any model has a Cook's distance above the median of F(p, n − p). With the standard deviation of the half of the predicted values in which each prediction lies, the judgement over the NOR is the same for both attributes (@sec-residuals).

## PD-003-05, duplicate univariate runs {#sec-pd-05}

The duplicate runs give the pooled standard deviation of the study, with `{python} UV_DF` degrees of freedom, against which each univariate difference was tested, including the effect of the initial viable cell concentration on acidic variants (@sec-univariate).

## PD-003-06, setting of osmolality {#sec-pd-06}

Because osmolality was set independently of pCO2, the screening design and the osmolality study estimate the two effects separately, and the PAR of pCO2 does not include the rise of osmolality that comes with pCO2 at scale (@sec-par-table).

# Appendix C. Full effect and coefficient tables {.unnumbered #sec-app-c}

@tbl-scr-afucosylation to @tbl-scr-aggregates give every effect of the screening models, in the factor codes of @tbl-factors. @tbl-coef-afucosylation to @tbl-anova-aggregates give the coefficients and the analysis of variance of the selected response-surface models of the attributes other than acidic variants, whose tables are in @sec-effects.

```{python}
#| output: asis
def scr_table(r):
    _d = SCRE[r].copy()
    for _c in ("Effect", "Coef.", "Std. err.", "t"):
        _d[_c] = _d[_c].map(lambda v: f"{v:.4f}".replace("-", "−"))
    _d["p-value"] = _d["p-value"].map(p3)
    return _d


for _r, _lab in zip(RESPS, ["afucosylation", "galactosylation", "high-mannose", "acidic-variants", "aggregates"]):
    print(md(scr_table(_r)))
    print()
    print(f": Effects of the screening model of {OUT[_r]}, as measured in the scale-down model. {{#tbl-scr-{_lab}}}")
    print()
```
